name: Sarcondina

facts.text: Level 65, 30,000 health, crowd-control immune, armour factor 350 with 20% absorb; resists 20% of melee and 30% of everything else; the jelly model at size 150; tether 3,800; faction Undead Servants of Morgana.
45% of her hits add a poison (80 matter every 4 s for 20 s) to a target that is not already poisoned.
While she fights, a 'Sarcondina's servant' (level 55-59, jelly model) comes up beside her every 25-40 s; the servants die when she dies or resets.
She walks home at full health when nobody is left on her aggro list; respawn is the epic-encounter interval.
Sarcondina as older than the lord, the marsh nobody farms, the orcs' line round her page and the Kulaclan's account of why the ones who ran stayed in the north are Living Server writing.

story:
Sarcondina is the marsh of Inishail, or the marsh is hers; the tenants of the isle never made the distinction. The reader of the old tongues who wrote the college's description of the island before the war saw a great slow shape move in the middle of it at evening, and smaller ones come to it, and asked the tenants whose the wet ground was. They said the marsh's, and the lord did not contradict them. Lord Emthoro held every other part of Inishail by walking it. He never walked the middle.

She is older than the lord and older than his line. The lammia of the south-west say she was there when the isles were one country and the sea had not come in, and that she was the low country's marsh then and has simply become smaller. She does not hunt. She does not need to. Whatever comes into the wet ground comes to her in the end, and the smaller slimes and oozes of the marsh, corrosive and viscous and congealed, are her kin and her household, and when she is troubled they come up out of the slime one after another to her side. Her touch clings and eats, and goes on eating after she has let go, though not for long; the slime does not keep its anger.

When the orcs who ran from Krondon's ogres crossed to Inishail, they tried first to farm the middle of the isle, because it was flat and wet and they were used to the Aldland shore. The Kulaclan, who stayed behind, tell what happened with some satisfaction: the ogres were only the reason the orcs left Aldland, and Sarcondina was the reason they ended up in the north-west, under the lord's door, which was worse. In the stolen tome in Toca's hut, on the page about the marsh, an orc has written SHE in the margin and drawn a careful line round the whole page.

Morgana's dead have reached the marsh too, and the witch counts Sarcondina among her own, as she counts everything on the isles that kills Albion's soldiers. The lammia say Sarcondina has not noticed. The slime is spreading toward the beaches and the north. The lammia say she has noticed that.
legend: Sarcondina, level 65, 30k health, in the slime marsh in the middle of Inishail. A slow melee fight with a steady stream of help: every 25 to 40 seconds a Sarcondina's servant (55-59) comes up next to her and joins in, so have someone pick each one up as it arrives or they stack on the healers. 45% of her hits put an 80 per tick poison on the target (20 seconds), so cure poison on the tank or heal through it. She cannot be mezzed or stunned. Her tether is long (3,800), so do not try to drag her out of the marsh. Servants die when she does. A wipe resets her to full and clears the servants; she respawns about an hour after she dies.

loremasterTopic.text: The marsh of [inishail island], or the marsh's; the tenants never made the distinction. Older than the lord, she does not hunt: whatever comes into the wet ground comes to her, and her smaller kin crawl up to her side when she is troubled. The orcs who ran from Krondon tried to farm her marsh once.

bookPage: From Of the Isle of Rest, the reader's description recovered from Toca's hut, with the orcs' margins. Of the marsh. The middle of the isle is a wet ground that the tenants do not farm, being someone else's. At evening a great slow shape moves in it, and smaller ones come to it from all sides, as a household comes in from the fields. The lord does not walk the middle, though he walks everything else. In the margin, in charcoal, in the heavy hand: SHE. Below it the orc has drawn a farm, a small one, with a fence. Then he has drawn the marsh over it. Then he has drawn a line round the whole page, very carefully, the way the old women of a village draw round a sick house.
